result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers catch the undefined --ref-slate-300, but B makes only that one-line fix, returns the file otherwise unchanged and leaves the dark-theme literals as a clearly optional suggestion. A goes further and invents ten new ref tokens and reorders the palette. Some of A's new names also run against their values: slate-300 is darker than slate-400, and teal-950 is lighter than teal-900. That adds confusion to a file that was meant only to be tidied for a handoff. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A fixes the undefined --ref-slate-300 with a single added line, says the hex value is a guess to check, and leaves everything else alone. It mentions the raw hex values in the dark block only as an optional follow-up it did not apply. B also fixes the bug but goes on to add 11 new ref tokens, rewrite the dark block and regroup the palette. Several of its new names misorder the ramp: slate-400 is lighter than slate-300, slate-500 and slate-600 are nearly identical, and teal-950 is lighter than teal-900. That contradicts B's own claim that it put the ramp in order.
